overview: Infratil is a New Zealand-based infrastructure investment company (NZX: IFT, ASX: IFT) with a market capitalisation of roughly NZ$12.5-16bn depending on the marking period, that owns and actively manages a portfolio of infrastructure assets across digital infrastructure, renewable energy, healthcare, telecommunications and airports. Operating across Australasia, North America, Asia and Europe, Infratil's portfolio value (NZ$20.6bn at 31 March 2026) is increasingly dominated by CDC Data Centres - a globally scaled AI/hyperscale data centre platform whose independent valuation jumped a further ~24% in the June 2026 quarter alone to A$18.5bn - alongside Longroad Energy, a US renewable developer, and consolidated subsidiaries One NZ (mobile/telco) and CDC. The company is externally managed by Morrison & Co and targets 11-15% annualised total shareholder returns over a rolling 10-year basis, having delivered 18.9% TSR since inception in 1994.

business_model.summary: Infratil generates returns through capital appreciation and distributions from its portfolio companies, funded by long-term contracted infrastructure revenues, and reports results on a Proportionate Operational EBITDAF basis (FY2026: NZ$989.4m) alongside statutory consolidated accounts (One NZ and CDC are consolidated subsidiaries). The company is externally managed by Morrison & Co under a management agreement that includes performance-based incentive fees. CDC Data Centres (data centre leasing) and Longroad Energy (renewable power generation and development) are the primary growth engines; One NZ (telecommunications), Wellington Airport, and healthcare assets provide more stable cash generation.

revenue_streams.trend: growing strongly - valuation +23.6% in the single June 2026 quarter

revenue_streams.trend: growing, though underlying USD valuation eased in Q1 FY27 on higher base rates

revenue_streams.trend: mixed - Galileo/Mint posted modest valuation gains at Q1 FY27

business_model.customer_type: Mix of B2B (data centres with hyperscaler/government tenants, wholesale energy, telecom infrastructure) and B2C (retail telecommunications, medical imaging, airport services)
business_model.geographic_mix: Australia 47%, New Zealand 32%, United States 13%, Europe 5%, Asia 3%
business_model.portfolio_structure: Three-pillar approach: Pillar 1 (cash generators: One NZ, Wellington Airport, healthcare) providing stable distributions; Pillar 2 (scaling growth: CDC, Longroad Energy) driving asset value uplift; Pillar 3 (early-stage platforms: Gurin Energy, Galileo, Mint Renewables, Kao Data, Clearvision) seeding future growth

main_competitors: Brookfield Asset Management (global infrastructure, including AirTrunk-scale data centre platforms)
AustralianSuper and other super fund direct infrastructure investment
competitive_position.market_position: Leading infrastructure investment company in New Zealand; included in S&P/NZX 50, ASX 200 (since July 2025), and MSCI Global Standard Index. Rated BBB+ (stable) by S&P since December 2025. CDC is the leading data centre operator in Australasia and is becoming a globally relevant AI infrastructure platform, with contracted capacity now exceeding 1GW and a leasable pipeline expanded to 3.9GW through FY2040.

moat_factors.factor: CDC's structural advantages in AI data centre supply
moat_factors.description: CDC's contracted capacity exceeds 1GW following the 555MW deal (announced 5 May 2026) and subsequent smaller contract wins; development pipeline expanded to 3.9GW through FY2040 (~A$20bn of implied further capex). Long-duration contracts (30+ year with renewal options) with investment-grade counterparties (hyperscalers, government) provide earnings visibility. CDC's Baa2 senior (Moody's) and Baa3 hybrid ratings, plus a A$1bn AMTN hybrid bond (June 2026, first rated corporate hybrid by a data centre operator in that market) and a further A$700m senior secured debt issuance (July 2026), demonstrate capital-market access that funds growth without proportional equity calls on Infratil.

moat_factors.factor: Long-term contracted revenue across the portfolio
moat_factors.description: Data centre contracts typically 10-30 years; renewable energy PPAs 15-25 years; regulated airport and telecom revenues. Provides strong downside protection and earnings predictability.

moat_factors.factor: Morrison & Co management expertise and origination
moat_factors.description: 30+ years of infrastructure investment experience across a global network. Established relationships with governments, hyperscalers, and institutional capital. Early mover advantage in CDC (2016 investment, 35.8% IRR) and Longroad (2016, 47.3% IRR) validates origination capability. The external-manager structure itself continues to draw shareholder scrutiny (raised again at the August 2026 AGM), which the Board defends by reference to an independent PwC value-for-money assessment.

One NZ holds mobile spectrum licenses (34% of NZ mobile spectrum, alongside Spark's 33% and 2degrees' 16%); Wellington Airport has a natural monopoly; CDC campuses benefit from power connections and planning approvals that are difficult to replicate; renewable projects hold development rights and grid connections. Government has proposed reallocating a portion of Spark/One NZ 2600MHz spectrum holdings to 2degrees to boost competition (July 2026), a mild erosion of this barrier for One NZ.

Inaugural BBB+ (S&P, December 2025) enables access to broader debt markets and improved borrowing terms. Capital bonds programme (IFT380, BBB-, 50% equity credit) closed 5 June 2026 upsized to NZ$200m (from an initial NZ$150m target) at an initial rate of 5.50% to first reset in June 2032, evidencing strong retail/institutional demand for Infratil's own paper.

weaknesses: High and rising concentration in CDC (roughly 40-49% of portfolio value depending on the valuation date) creates single-asset sensitivity to AI demand cycles, hyperscaler capex decisions, and execution risk

New Zealand economic exposure across One NZ, Wellington Airport, healthcare assets and RHCNZ (~32% of geographic exposure), compounded by domestic passenger declines at Wellington Airport (5.1m travellers FY26, down from 5.3m) and only modest One NZ EBITDAF growth

External management structure incurs both base management fees and performance-based incentive fees that reduce net returns, and remains a recurring point of shareholder contention (raised again at the FY2026 AGM, 18 August 2026)

Corporate net debt increased to NZ$3.2 billion (LTV 15.4%) at FY26 year end, materially higher than NZ$2.2 billion in FY25, increasing interest burden even as underlying asset valuations (CDC in particular) have since risen further
Smaller scale than global mega-funds; share price has recently traded at a discount to both consensus analyst targets and to reported NAV per share, despite the CDC valuation surge

growth_drivers: CDC AI data centre supercycle accelerating further post-FY26: contracted capacity now exceeds 1GW after the 555MW deal (5 May 2026) plus subsequent smaller contract wins; CDC's independent valuation rose a further 23.6% in the June 2026 quarter alone to A$18.5bn, with the leasable development pipeline expanded from 2.6GW to 3.9GW through FY2040 (~A$20bn of implied incremental capital investment). CDC targets A$680-720m EBITDAF in FY27 (+73-83% on FY26), exceeding A$1bn in FY28, with fully deployed 1GW contracted capacity expected to generate ~A$2bn annualised EBITDAF.

CDC capital markets execution: CDC completed a A$1bn AMTN hybrid bond in June 2026 (Baa3, Moody's, 50% equity credit) - the first rated corporate hybrid issued by a data centre operator in that market - followed by a A$700m dual-tranche senior secured debt issuance in July 2026, funding the accelerated build programme (CDC net debt rose to A$5,976m) largely without further proportional equity calls on Infratil.

Longroad Energy US renewable acceleration, though the underlying US-dollar valuation eased slightly at the Q1 FY27 (30 June 2026) valuation update on lower inflation assumptions and higher base rates. Longroad closed FY26 with 3.5GW operational, 2GW under construction, and agreed to acquire a ~2.8GW solar and storage project (subject to regulatory approvals). Infratil committed a further US$300m over two years to support this step-up. Longroad targets ~US$490m Opco run-rate EBITDAF in CY26 and US$1bn by CY29/30.

Longroad data centre co-location strategy: Longroad is actively developing options for 4GW+ of grid-connected data centres co-located with its solar and storage assets, creating a new revenue stream at the intersection of its renewable and digital infrastructure capabilities.

Portfolio divestment and capital recycling continuing: NZ$600m of asset sales completed in FY26 (Manawa to Contact, RetireAustralia NZ$331m, Infratil Property NZ$55m, Fortysouth >NZ$200m). NZ$495m raised from a May 2026 block-trade sale of 5% of Contact Energy, reducing the stake to ~9%; Infratil had committed to holding that residual stake at least through Contact's FY26 results (expected on/around 18 August 2026) - whether it has since been further reduced was not confirmed in available reporting. Qscan sale process remains underway with an update still expected; management continues to flag potential for another NZ$1bn+ of medium-term divestments.

Kao Data UK expansion: Revenue grew 28% to £48m in FY26. New 30MW+ West London greenfield site acquired, targeted for 2029 delivery. KLON-03 (17.6MW, GPU-optimised) under construction with capacity online from early 2027. Materially all current capacity contracted.

Broadening shareholder base: ASX 200 inclusion (July 2025) has lifted ASX trading volume to ~30% of total, with growing Australian institutional ownership and expanded analyst coverage (Goldman Sachs initiated Buy, NZ$17.60 target). These factors support valuation discovery and could narrow the persistent NAV/market-price discount.

Board refresh: Brad Banducci (former Woolworths Group CEO) elected to the Board and Tiffany Fuller appointed post the August 2026 AGM, alongside the retirement of long-serving director Peter Springford, refreshing governance as the portfolio's scale and complexity (CDC, Longroad) grows.

business.description: CDC represented approximately 43% of portfolio asset value at the FY26 balance date (NZ$8.9bn) and has grown further since - CDC's own independent valuation reached ~A$18.5bn (Infratil's ~49.7% stake ~A$9.2bn/NZ$11.2bn) at 30 June 2026, pushing CDC's share of total portfolio value toward ~40-50% depending on how other assets are marked concurrently. A disappointment in AI data centre demand - hyperscaler capex pullbacks, alternative compute architectures, oversupply, or execution delays on contracted capacity - could have an outsized negative impact on Infratil's NAV and share price.

While contract momentum and valuation gains have continued through mid-2026 (pipeline expanded to 3.9GW through FY2040, underpinned by hyperscaler capex plans reported around US$650bn for 2026), the AI infrastructure build-out is unprecedented in scale and speed. Market commentary already flags 'AI-driven volatility' around Infratil's share price even as CDC's own valuation rises, indicating investor nervousness about the durability of hyperscaler demand and the risk of efficiency breakthroughs curbing future contract signings.

Persistent macroeconomic headwinds in NZ affect One NZ (EBITDAF grew only modestly at NZ$609m, essentially flat in real terms), Wellington Airport (total passengers fell to 5.1m in FY26 from 5.3m, domestic softness only partly offset by 4% international growth), and healthcare imaging volumes. NZ accounts for roughly 32% of geographic exposure.

Galileo recognised write-offs and write-downs of €61.2m (IFT share €23.3m) in FY26 as early-stage development values fell across European markets moving to maturity. The Q1 FY27 (30 June 2026) valuation update showed only a modest underlying uplift, suggesting the reset toward fewer markets and an independent power producer model is still in early stages of proving out. IRR has been modest (9.9% over 6 years).

business.risk: Gurin Energy - Project Vanda approval uncertainty
business.description: Project Vanda (2GW Indonesian solar, subsea export to Singapore; US$2-3bn capex) obtained Indonesia's production licence in March 2026 but is still awaiting the export licence as the key gate to final investment decision. No confirmed update on this approval was found in reporting through August 2026; prolonged delays risk stranding development capital and opportunity cost.

financial.description: Infratil's corporate net debt increased from NZ$2.2bn to NZ$3.2bn in FY26, driven by the A$500m CDC equity injection (February 2026) and Contact Energy acquisition costs. LTV ratio rose to 15.4% (from 12.8%) at 31 March 2026. Although the BBB+ credit rating provides access to capital markets - demonstrated by the oversubscribed NZ$200m capital bond issue in June 2026 at 5.50% - elevated debt increases interest costs. Weighted average cost of drawn debt was 5.20% with a short average tenor of 2.7 years at FY26 year end.

Approximately 65% of portfolio value is in offshore assets denominated in AUD, USD, GBP and EUR. CDC and Qscan (AUD), Longroad (USD), Kao Data (GBP), and Galileo/Gurin (USD/EUR). NZD strength would reduce the NZD value of offshore earnings and asset valuations. The Q1 FY27 Longroad update illustrated this directly: Longroad's NZD-reported valuation rose even as its underlying USD value fell, reflecting FX translation effects offsetting weaker fundamentals.

Resolved favourably since the FY26 result: Infratil's inaugural capital bonds (IFT380, BBB-, 50% equity credit) closed 5 June 2026, upsized to NZ$200m from an initial NZ$150m target (including NZ$50m of oversubscriptions) at an initial rate of 5.50% to first reset (15 June 2032). Demonstrates continued access to diversified funding, though the coupon reflects a still-elevated rate environment relative to Infratil's blended cost of debt.

Infratil has committed US$300m (approximately NZ$520m at guidance rates) to Longroad over the next ~2 years on top of existing commitments. This is a large call on capital that will need to be funded through asset divestments, operating distributions, and/or debt, at the same time Longroad's underlying USD valuation has softened on higher base-rate assumptions.

regulatory.risk: US renewable energy policy - OBBBA tightening of IRA credits
regulatory.description: The One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA, enacted 2025) has materially tightened the prior Inflation Reduction Act timeline: solar and wind projects that begin construction after 4 July 2026 lose Section 48E investment tax credit eligibility unless placed in service by 31 December 2027, and the residential Section 25D credit terminated for expenditures after 31 December 2025. New FEOC (foreign entity of concern) sourcing restrictions add compliance risk from 2026. This is a materially firmer and nearer-dated constraint on Longroad's development economics than the general 'IRA framework' risk previously described, and coincides with Longroad's own valuation easing in the Q1 FY27 update on higher base rates.

One NZ is subject to Commerce Commission oversight on pricing, spectrum, and infrastructure sharing. In July 2026 the NZ government proposed reallocating a share of Spark's and One NZ's 2600MHz spectrum holdings to 2degrees to boost competition, a concrete near-term regulatory development that could dilute One NZ's spectrum-based competitive position (One NZ currently holds ~34% of overall mobile spectrum versus Spark's 33% and 2degrees' 16%).

Wellington Airport aeronautical pricing is reviewed by the Commerce Commission. Input methodologies and price path determinations constrain revenue growth. Current BBB (S&P, stable) rating supports access to capital at competitive rates.

Increasing data localisation requirements and potential AI-specific regulation could affect CDC's customer mix, facility requirements, or operational model. Australia's National AI Plan currently identifies CDC-style infrastructure as foundational, but regulatory evolution could change incentive structures.

macro.risk: Interest rate and discount rate sensitivity
macro.description: Infrastructure assets are valued using discounted cash flow models. The Q1 FY27 CDC valuation update explicitly noted a 25bp rise in the assumed long-term risk-free rate, lifting CDC's cost of equity from 11.84% to 12.45% - a direct illustration that even as growth assumptions improve, higher discount rates are a persistent offsetting force on valuation. Infratil's own weighted average cost of debt was 5.20% with a short 2.7-year average tenor at FY26 year end, creating refinancing risk if rates remain elevated, though the June 2026 capital bond priced acceptably at 5.50%.

CDC's growth ambitions depend on procuring sufficient grid-connected power in Australia. Delays in grid upgrades, constraints on power procurement, or higher-than-expected electricity costs could slow CDC's build programme or compress margins. CDC's WUE of less than 0.02 and 100% renewable electricity offering mitigate some constraint risk, but the pipeline expansion to 3.9GW through FY2040 significantly raises the scale of power procurement required.

US tariff policies affect the cost of solar panels, batteries, and data centre equipment imported for Longroad and CDC/Longroad projects. Higher equipment costs could impair project economics, particularly for large-scale solar developments with construction starting from CY28, and interact with the OBBBA's tightened placed-in-service deadlines to compress the window for qualifying projects.

Wellington Airport and NZ assets are exposed to seismic and weather risks. The completed runway safety upgrade (EMAS system, March 2026) now enables long-haul flights to Asia, though no confirmed long-haul routes had been announced as of the FY26 result. Hydro generation and renewables are exposed to changing precipitation patterns.

execution.risk: CDC delivery execution at an accelerating scale
execution.description: Delivering 1GW+ of contracted capacity plus a pipeline now expanded to 3.9GW through FY2040 is an unprecedented and still-accelerating build programme for CDC. CDC net debt rose to A$5,976m to fund this, alongside the new A$1bn hybrid and A$700m senior secured debt issuances. Delays in construction, power procurement, or customer activation would defer the associated EBITDAF ramp and could pressure the elevated valuation multiple the market and independent valuers are now applying.

The Qscan sale process remains underway with no confirmed completion as of late August 2026, in a challenging M&A environment; closing at book value is not guaranteed. Infratil's commitment to hold its residual ~9% Contact Energy stake through at least Contact's FY26 result (expected ~18 August 2026) means the next step in that capital recycling was not yet confirmed in available reporting.

RHCNZ Medical Imaging EBITDAF was flat at NZ$63.6m while valuation declined NZ$73m to NZ$616m at FY26, reflecting challenging trading conditions, cost pressures and revised long-term growth assumptions. A performance improvement programme is underway but the IRR since inception of 8.6% is below Infratil's targets.

execution.risk: Management incentive fee structure and external-manager scrutiny
execution.description: In FY26, incentive fee calculations produced a net negative position (NZ$39.4m), as outperformance at CDC was more than offset by underperformance at Galileo, Gurin, Longroad and others; this carries forward to reduce future payables. However, given CDC's subsequent valuation surge in Q1 FY27, future incentive-fee crystallisation could become material again. Shareholders continued to challenge the external-manager model directly at the August 2026 AGM (at a now much larger ~NZ$12.5-16bn market cap), with the Board defending the arrangement by reference to an independent PwC assessment rather than committing to internalisation.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global infrastructure investment is benefiting from structural megatrends: AI and cloud computing driving unprecedented data centre demand (hyperscaler 2026 capex plans reported around US$650bn); decarbonisation driving renewable energy investment, now complicated in the US by the OBBBA's tightened tax-credit deadlines; and government infrastructure deficits creating private capital opportunities. The AI data centre build-out remains a multi-year demand supercycle for digital infrastructure assets, evidenced by CDC's pipeline expansion to 3.9GW through FY2040, though commentary increasingly flags valuation and 'AI-driven volatility' debate around how much of this growth is already priced in.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Low to moderate. The portfolio is structured to provide downside protection through long-term contracts (data centres, PPAs) and regulated/monopoly assets (airport, telecom), while CDC and Longroad provide significant upside to the AI/energy transition thematic. Economic sensitivity is meaningful through One NZ consumer revenues, Wellington Airport domestic traffic (which fell in FY26), and healthcare volumes.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High - both directly (Infratil's NZ$3.2bn corporate net debt at 5.20% weighted average cost, refreshed with a NZ$200m capital bond at 5.50% in June 2026) and indirectly (discount rates compress infrastructure asset valuations when rates are elevated - CDC's own cost of equity rose from 11.84% to 12.45% in the June 2026 valuation update on a 25bp risk-free rate increase, even as growth assumptions improved).
macro_factors.currency_exposure: Significant - approximately 65% of portfolio is in offshore assets (AUD ~47%, USD ~13%, GBP/EUR ~5%). NZD movements affect the translated value of offshore earnings and asset valuations; the Q1 FY27 Longroad update showed NZD-reported value rising even as underlying USD value fell, illustrating this effect can mask or amplify underlying performance.
key_input_costs: Electricity (data centre operations - CDC passes through or hedges power costs)
Construction materials and equipment (solar panels, batteries, data centre build-out - exposed to both tariffs and OBBBA sourcing/FEOC restrictions)
Interest rates and risk-free rate assumptions (debt funding and DCF discount rates across Infratil parent and all portfolio companies)
Technology equipment (servers, GPUs, telecom network gear - tariff sensitive)

recent_developments.event: 32nd Annual Shareholder Meeting held 18 August 2026 (Wellington, hybrid). Chair confirmed FY27 guidance unchanged; noted NZ businesses were 'largely constrained by ongoing softness in the domestic economy' while Longroad and CDC are 'experiencing exceptional demand.' Board changes: Peter Springford retired after almost a decade; Brad Banducci (former Woolworths Group CEO) elected; Tiffany Fuller appointed post-meeting. Shareholder questions again challenged the external-manager structure and KPMG's 25-year audit tenure; no changes announced to either.

CDC independent valuation update (30 June 2026): CDC's overall enterprise value rose 23.6% quarter-on-quarter to a A$18.5bn midpoint; Infratil's ~49.7% stake increased to ~A$9.2bn (~NZ$11.2bn), a gain of ~A$1.76bn (NZ$2.14bn) in the quarter. Driven by contracted capacity surpassing 1GW and pipeline expansion from 2.6GW to 3.9GW through FY2040 (~A$20bn of implied further capex). CDC's assessed cost of equity nonetheless rose from 11.84% to 12.45% on a 25bp increase in the long-term risk-free rate. CDC net debt rose to A$5,976m.

Separate valuation update for Longroad Energy, Galileo and Mint Renewables as at 30 June 2026 (Qscan excluded, pending its strategic review): Longroad's NZD-reported valuation rose but its underlying USD value declined on lower inflation assumptions and higher base rates; Galileo and Mint Renewables both posted modest underlying uplifts.
CDC completed a A$700m dual-tranche senior secured debt issuance in the AMTN market - the first senior debt issuance by a data centre operator in that market - following the June hybrid bond.

CDC issued a A$1bn corporate hybrid bond in two tranches via the AMTN market (Baa3, Moody's; 50% equity credit) - the first rated corporate hybrid issued by a data centre operator in that market - funding the accelerated build programme.

Infratil completed its inaugural capital bond offer (IFT380): opened 2 June, closed 5 June, allocated NZ$200m (upsized from an initial NZ$150m target, including NZ$50m of oversubscriptions) at an initial interest rate of 5.50% p.a. to the first reset date (15 June 2032). Listed on the NZX Debt Market 16 June 2026.

Post-balance date: sold 5% stake in Contact Energy (53.5m shares at NZ$9.25) via fully underwritten block trade, raising ~NZ$495m. Reduced Contact holding to ~9%. Infratil committed to retaining the remaining stake at least until Contact's FY26 results (expected on/around 18 August 2026); no confirmed update on any further sale was found in available reporting.

FY2026 annual results announced 26 May 2026: Proportionate Operational EBITDAF NZ$989m (+11%), total asset/portfolio value NZ$20.6bn (+13%), NAV NZ$16.26/share (+5%). Net parent surplus NZ$549.8m. FY27 EBITDAF guidance NZ$1,300-1,400m issued (implying ~21% increase); reaffirmed unchanged as of the August 2026 AGM. Final dividend brought full-year FY2026 dividend to 20.9 cents per share (+2% YoY).

CDC announced a 555MW data centre contract (5 May 2026) with an unnamed US investment-grade customer on a 30-year term (plus 20-year renewal options) - Australia's largest-ever data centre contract, lifting CDC's total contracted capacity beyond 1GW. CDC was assigned a Baa2 (stable) senior credit rating by Moody's on 21 April 2026.

Longroad Energy agreed to acquire a ~2.8GW solar and battery storage development project in the US, subject to state regulatory approvals; Infratil committed additional US$300m equity to support Longroad's accelerated ~2GW-per-annum development cadence, targeting US$1bn run-rate EBITDAF by CY29/30.

guidance.management_commentary: At the FY2026 result, CEO Jason Boyes described CDC as having a 'once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to develop AI infrastructure at globally relevant scale.' At the 18 August 2026 AGM, the Chair confirmed FY27 guidance 'remains unchanged' and characterised NZ operating businesses as constrained by domestic economic softness while Longroad and CDC continue to see 'exceptional demand.' Market commentary through July 2026 (e.g., Simply Wall St, Kalkine) increasingly frames the investment debate around how much of CDC's growth is already reflected in Infratil's share price versus its portfolio value, given the scale of the June-quarter valuation jump.

bull_case: CDC earnings and valuation supercycle continuing to surprise to the upside: CDC's independent valuation rose a further 23.6% in the June 2026 quarter alone (to A$18.5bn) on top of the FY26 uplift, with the leasable pipeline expanded to 3.9GW through FY2040. CDC EBITDAF is set to compound from A$393m in FY26 to A$680-720m in FY27 and exceed A$1bn in FY28; fully deployed 1GW contracted capacity equates to ~A$2bn annualised EBITDAF.

Proven capital-markets access de-risks the build programme: CDC's A$1bn hybrid bond (June 2026) and A$700m senior secured issuance (July 2026) - both firsts for a data centre operator in the AMTN market - show CDC can fund its accelerating capex largely through debt rather than repeated calls on Infratil equity, while Infratil's own oversubscribed NZ$200m capital bond (5.50%, June 2026) demonstrates continued market confidence in the parent credit.

Portfolio rerating potential remains open: Despite the CDC valuation surge, commentary through mid-2026 notes Infratil's share price has traded at a discount to both consensus analyst targets (NZ$17-17.6, e.g. Goldman Sachs Buy) and to reported NAV, suggesting the market has not yet fully re-rated to reflect CDC's underlying asset value - a gap that could close as ASX 200 inclusion and Australian institutional ownership continue to build.

Strong track record of value creation with proven management: 18.9% annualised TSR since 1994 inception. Morrison & Co's 30+ year infrastructure track record and early mover positions in CDC (35.8% IRR) and Longroad (47.3% IRR) demonstrate exceptional origination discipline. FY27 EBITDAF guidance of NZ$1.3-1.4bn was explicitly reaffirmed 'unchanged' at the August 2026 AGM despite NZ economic softness.

Balance sheet now investment grade with multiple, recently-proven capital avenues: BBB+ (S&P) parent rating, CDC Baa2 senior / Baa3 hybrid (Moody's), Wellington Airport BBB (S&P). Both the parent capital bond and CDC's hybrid/senior debt issuances in June-July 2026 were completed successfully (the parent bond upsized on demand), evidencing genuine, not just theoretical, funding flexibility.
bear_case: CDC concentration risk is rising, not falling: CDC's share of portfolio value has grown further since FY26 (43%) given the additional ~A$1.76bn quarterly valuation gain in June 2026, and 'AI-driven volatility' is now an explicit theme in market commentary on the stock. If hyperscaler capex moderates, technology efficiency gains reduce compute demand, or delivery on the expanded 3.9GW pipeline disappoints, the impact on Infratil's NAV would be severe with limited portfolio diversification to offset it.

Discount-rate risk cuts against the growth story: even in the same July 2026 update that lifted CDC's valuation, the independent valuer raised CDC's cost of equity from 11.84% to 12.45% on a 25bp rise in the assumed risk-free rate - a reminder that further increases in long-term rates could materially compress the multiple applied to CDC's cash flows, independent of operating performance.

US renewables policy has tightened materially: the OBBBA now requires solar/wind projects to begin construction by 4 July 2026 and be placed in service by 31 December 2027 to retain full ITC eligibility, with new FEOC sourcing restrictions adding compliance risk. This is a nearer-dated and more concrete constraint on Longroad's ~2GW-per-annum development cadence and the pending 2.8GW acquisition than the prior general 'IRA framework' risk, and coincides with Longroad's own USD asset value easing in the Q1 FY27 update.

Corporate net debt and short tenor still create refinancing vulnerability: net debt grew from NZ$2.2bn to NZ$3.2bn (+46%) in FY26 with only a 2.7-year weighted average tenor; the parent capital bond priced at 5.50%, above the FY26 average cost of debt, illustrating that new funding is not necessarily cheaper even for an investment-grade issuer.

External-manager governance overhang persists: shareholders again challenged the Morrison & Co external management structure and the 25-year KPMG audit relationship at the August 2026 AGM without securing changes, and CDC's valuation surge raises the prospect of large incentive-fee crystallisation in future periods (FY26's fee was a rare net-negative NZ$39.4m) - a recurring source of investor friction that a pure operating-company structure would not carry.
